label: The Satya (Krita) Yuga
summary: First of the four ages. Tradition says it lasts 1,728,000 years counting dawn and dusk, and that dharma stands on all four legs. The figures differ by text and are a traditional reckoning, not a count of years.

label: Dharma as a bull on four legs
summary: The Bhagavata Purana pictures dharma as a bull. In this age it stands on all four legs, named austerity, cleanliness, compassion and truth. Each later age removes one.
verification: web (one source); tradition, primary text not read

label: An age without buying or selling
summary: The Mahabharata describes the first age as one with no trade, no rich or poor, little illness and no hatred. It is a literary ideal and is not offered as history.
verification: web (one source); tradition, primary text not read

label: One Veda before the four
summary: The Bhagavata Purana says that in the first age there was a single Veda and one mantra, Om, and that the Veda was later divided into four.
verification: web (one source); tradition, primary text not read

label: Matsya, the fish avatar
summary: In the common list of ten avatars, Matsya, the fish form of Vishnu, comes first and is placed in the Satya age. Accounts differ by text on what he does.
verification: web (one source); tradition, primary text not read

label: Kurma, the tortoise avatar
summary: Kurma, the tortoise form of Vishnu, is second in the common list and is placed in the Satya age. He is linked to the story of the churning of the ocean.
verification: web (one source); tradition, primary text not read

label: The churning of the ocean
summary: Puranic accounts tell of beings pulling a great serpent-rope around a mountain to churn the ocean. Where it sits among the ages varies by text, and the game only mentions it.

label: Varaha, the boar avatar
summary: Varaha, the boar form of Vishnu, is third in the common list and is placed in the Satya age. The Puranas tell of him raising the earth from the waters.
verification: web (one source); tradition, primary text not read

label: Narasimha, the man-lion avatar
summary: Narasimha is fourth in the common list and is placed in the Satya age. The story honours Prahlada, a child whose steady devotion is the heart of the tale.
verification: web (one source); tradition, primary text not read

label: Duration of the dawn and dusk of Satya
summary: Texts give each twilight of the first age as 144,000 years, within a 4:3:2:1 ratio between the four ages. The ratio and figures come from the Surya Siddhanta and Puranas.
verification: web (one source); tradition, primary text not read

label: The four ages differ in text and in count
summary: Authors differ on yuga lengths. The 4,320,000-year four-age cycle is stated in the Surya Siddhanta; a day of Brahma is a thousand such cycles in the Bhagavata Purana.
